title: Differential Equations
description: Class 12 IMO — Differential Equations: order and degree, formation of differential equations, variable-separable equations, and linear differential equations.

topics.title: Order, Degree and Formation
topics.concept:
A differential equation relates a function to its derivatives. For example $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2x$ or $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}+y=0$.

Order and degree

  • The order is the order of the highest derivative present.
  • The degree is the power of the highest-order derivative, after the equation is made free of radicals and fractions in the derivatives. Degree is defined only when the equation is polynomial in its derivatives.

For instance, $\left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^3+\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0$ has order $2$ and degree $3$.

General and particular solutions

A solution containing arbitrary constants is the general solution; fixing the constants using given conditions gives a particular solution. An $n$th-order equation has $n$ arbitrary constants in its general solution.

Forming a differential equation

Given a family of curves with $n$ arbitrary constants, differentiate $n$ times and eliminate the constants. The result is a differential equation of order $n$ that the whole family satisfies.

examples.problem: Find the order and degree of $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}+3\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2+y=0$.
examples.solution: Highest derivative is $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ (order $2$); its power is $1$, so degree $1$.

examples.problem: Find the order and degree of $\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^3+2y=x$.
examples.solution: Highest derivative is first order; its highest power is $3$. Order $1$, degree $3$.

examples.problem: Form the differential equation of the family $y=mx$ ($m$ arbitrary).
Verify that $y=e^{2x}$ is a solution of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2y$.
examples.solution: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2e^{2x}=2y$. The equation is satisfied, so $y=e^{2x}$ is a solution.

recap: Order = highest derivative present; degree = power of that derivative (polynomial form).
General solution has $n$ arbitrary constants for order $n$; particular solution fixes them.
To form a DE from a family with $n$ constants: differentiate $n$ times, eliminate constants.
Verify a solution by substituting it back into the equation.

topics.title: Variable-Separable Equations
topics.concept:
A first-order equation is variable-separable if it can be written so that all the $y$-terms (with $dy$) are on one side and all the $x$-terms (with $dx$) on the other:

$$\frac{dy}{dx}=g(x)\,h(y)\ \Longrightarrow\ \frac{dy}{h(y)}=g(x)\,dx.$$

Then integrate both sides. A single constant of integration $C$ captures the family.

Method

  1. Separate the variables.
  2. Integrate each side.
  3. Combine constants into one $C$.
  4. Apply any initial condition to find $C$ for a particular solution.
recap: Combine all constants into a single $C$.
Use an initial condition to pin down $C$.

quiz.q: The particular solution of dy/dx = 2x, given that y(1) = 2, is:
quiz.explanation: dy = 2x dx. Integrating gives y = x² + C. At x=1, y=2 → 2 = (1)² + C → C = 1. So, y = x² + 1.

topics.title: Linear Differential Equations
topics.concept:
A first-order linear differential equation has the standard form

$$\frac{dy}{dx}+P(x)\,y=Q(x),$$

where $P$ and $Q$ are functions of $x$ only. It is solved using an integrating factor.

The integrating factor (IF)

$$\text{IF}=e^{\int P\,dx}.$$

Multiplying through by the IF turns the left side into the derivative of (IF $\times y$). The solution is then

$$y\cdot(\text{IF})=\int Q\cdot(\text{IF})\,dx + C.$$

Method

  1. Put the equation in standard form and read off $P$ and $Q$.
  2. Compute IF $=e^{\int P\,dx}$.
  3. Write $y\cdot\text{IF}=\int Q\cdot\text{IF}\,dx+C$ and integrate.

examples.solution: IF $=x$. Then $y\cdot x=\int x\cdot x\,dx=\int x^2 dx=\dfrac{x^3}{3}+C$. So $y=\dfrac{x^2}{3}+\dfrac{C}{x}.$

recap: Always put the equation in standard form before reading $P$ and $Q$.

quiz.q: An object cools according to dT/dt=−0.5(T−20). If T=20°C, then dT/dt equals:
A water tank leaks water at a rate proportional to the square root of the volume V of water remaining. The differential equation is:
quiz.explanation: Leaking means the volume is decreasing over time. Proportional to square root of V means dV/dt = −k√V (where k is a positive constant).

questions.q: In a culture, the bacteria count is 100,000. The number is increasing at a rate proportional to the number present. In 2 hours, it increases by 10%. The DE is dN/dt = kN. What is N at time t=0?
questions.explanation: The initial count at t=0 is explicitly given in the problem as 100,000.

questions.q: Solution of the differential equation (x + y) dy − dx = 0 is:
questions.explanation: dx/dy = x + y → dx/dy − x = y. This is a linear DE in x. IF = e^(∫−1 dy) = e⁻ʸ. Solution: x(e⁻ʸ) = ∫y e⁻ʸ dy + C. Integrating by parts: −y e⁻ʸ − e⁻ʸ + c. Multiply by eʸ: x = −y − 1 + C eʸ, which is x + y + 1 = C eʸ.

questions.q: The solution of dy/dx=(x+y)/x can be obtained using:
Find the general solution of the differential equation x dy + y dx = 0.
questions.explanation: x dy = −y dx → dy/y = −dx/x. Integrating gives log y = −log x + log C → log(xy) = log C → xy = C.

questions.q: Which method is most appropriate to solve dy/dx = (x + y)²?
questions.explanation: The equation is not homogeneous or linear, and variables cannot be separated directly. Letting x + y = v gives 1 + dy/dx = dv/dx, so dv/dx = v² + 1, which reduces it to variable separable form.

questions.q: The order of the differential equation representing the family of curves y = a sin(x + b), where a and b are arbitrary constants, is:
questions.explanation: There are two independent arbitrary constants (a and b) in the given family of curves. Hence, the differential equation will be of order 2.

The integrating factor (I.F.) of the linear differential equation dy/dx + Py = Q is given by:
questions.explanation: By definition, for a first-order linear differential equation in y, dy/dx + Py = Q, the integrating factor is e^(∫P dx).

questions.q: Rahul deposits ₹10,000 in a bank that pays interest compounded continuously at a rate of r% per annum. The differential equation for the principal P is:
questions.explanation: Continuous compounding means the rate of change of principal is proportional to the principal. dP/dt = (r/100)P.

questions.q: The differential equation dy/dx = y is:
questions.explanation: It can be written as dy/y = dx, hence variable separable.

questions.q: The solution of dy/dx = eˣ is:
The order of the differential equation d⁴y/dx⁴ + (d²y/dx²)² = 0 is:
questions.explanation: Highest derivative present is fourth order.

questions.q: The appropriate substitution to solve the homogeneous differential equation dx/dy = f(x/y) is:
questions.explanation: When the equation is expressed as dx/dy = f(x/y), it is easier to substitute x = vy, which gives dx/dy = v + y(dv/dy).
